title: Long-Lasting Antibodies for Immune Diseases: Cameron Turtle on The Long Run - TimmermanReport.com

text:
23Sep2026

Cameron Turtle is today’s guest on The Long Run.
Cameron Turtle, CEO, Spyre Therapeutics
Cameron is the CEO of Waltham, Mass.-based Spyre Therapeutics. The company is developing antibody drug candidates that are engineered to be longer-lasting than today’s drugs for immune disorders.
This means patients could take fewer injections and the drugs should stay stable in the bloodstream to keep the disease under control longer. Crucially, it opens the door for combinations of antibodies that could raise the bar on efficacy higher than any single drug can do for immune disorders and do it in a relatively straightforward treatment regimen that patients can stick with.
Spyre was spun out in 2023 from an antibody discovery shop called Paragon Therapeutics, which itself was founded by Fairmount Funds, a hedge fund, in 2021. The team created a set of antibody drug candidates against targets that are well-validated by others in clinical trials, and which represents a series of billion-dollar opportunities. Spyre’s portfolio includes antibodies aimed at alpha4 beta7, TL1A, and the p19 subunit of IL-23.
They are being tested as single agents and in combinations to tamp down excessive inflammation in patients with inflammatory bowel disease.
Investors like the company’s prospects. Spyre had $1.1 billion in cash at the time of this recording to fund a wide-ranging clinical development program. Its current market valuation is about $8 billion.
